parts.text: In this experiment, you will determine the density of a wooden block by two different methods. Refer to Figure 1.1. Method 1

ms.label: 1(a)(i)
ms.text:
all dimensions present
all values recorded to the nearest millimetre

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate the volume V B of the wooden block. Use the equation: V B = l × w × h. V B = .................................................. cm 3 [1]

parts.label: i
parts.text: (b) (i) Use the balance provided to measure the mass M of the block to the nearest gram. M = ...................................................... g [1]

ms.label: 1(b)(i)
ms.text: M recorded to the nearest g

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate a value ρ 1 for the density of the block. Use your results from 1(a)(ii) and 1(b)(i) and the equation: ρ 1 = M V B . ρ 1 = .............................................. g / cm 3 [1] Method 2 You are provided with two beakers, X and Y. Each beaker contains 200 cm 3 of water. You are also provided with a measuring cylinder containing water.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (c) (i) Measure the initial volume V 1 of water in the measuring cylinder. V 1 = .................................................. cm 3 [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) • Place the wooden block onto the surface of the water in beaker X. The level of the water in beaker X rises as the wooden block displaces water and floats. • Place beaker Y as close as possible to beaker X. • Slowly pour water from the measuring cylinder into beaker Y until the level of the water in beaker Y is the same as the level of the water in beaker X. Measure the volume V 2 of water remaining in the measuring cylinder. V 2 = ........................................................ cm 3 Determine a value for the volume V of water displaced by the block. Use the equation: V = V 1 – V 2 . V = ........................................................ cm 3 [1]

ms.label: 1(c)(ii)
ms.text: V2 present and V calculation correct

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) A second value ρ 2 for the density of the block can be calculated using the equation: ρ 2 = kV V B where k = 1.0 g / cm 3 . Use your answers to 1(c)(ii) and 1(a)(ii) to calculate ρ 2 . ρ 2 = .............................................. g / cm 3 [1]

parts.label: e
parts.text: (e) Two quantities can be considered to be equal within the limits of experimental accuracy if their values are within 10% of each other. State whether your values of ρ 1 from method 1 and ρ 2 from method 2 can be considered equal. Support your statement with a calculation. calculation statement ..................................................................................................................................
